newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian farm numbers fall, size increases-ABARE.
newsitem.headline: Australian farm numbers fall, size increases-ABARE.

text.p: Australian farm numbers have been declining but farms have been getting larger in the past 10 years, the Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics (ABARE) said in a report released on Tuesday.

Structural adjustment in Australia's farm sector had been occurring progressively rather than as a result of catastrophic events, Stephen Beare, ABARE's acting executive director, said releasing a report, Changing structure of farming in Australia.
Farm numbers had been declining gradually at the rate of just over one percent a year for the past 10 years due to the amalgamation of farms and increasing farm sizes, he said.
As farms increased in size, the probability of their being lost to agriculture generally fell, he said.
The study showed that the number of farms in Australia fell to 115,368 in 1994/95 from 130,281 in 1985/86.
The cut-off in annual income for inclusion in the count was A$22,500 in 1994/95.
The study also found new farm numbers were low, with only about two percent of farms in the broadacre and dairy industries being new farms.
The proportion was slightly higher in the horticulture industries, he said. -- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
